yarn-troppo.meaning: Every guideline survives: "Cold tucker goes in an esky with ice or frozen ice bricks, and it's got to sit at 40 °F (4 °C) or below", drinks and perishables in separate eskies, "Raw meat, chook and seafood stay wrapped up tight", the washing rules and the "triple washed" exception, marinating "in the fridge", partial cooking, the thermometer, the clean platter. Additions elaborate: "the one full of tinnies and half a bag of ice", "like your watermelon", "Not half-cooked at home and then an hour in the car."
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "esky", "chook", "ice bricks", "kitchen bench", "tea towel", "keep yourself, the family and your mates off the dunny", "that's how you end up crook", "the little mongrels multiply quick smart".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Largely a real voice ("every man and his dog can be in and out of the drinks esky topping up all arvo", "Here's the good oil"), but some tags are bolted on: "Beauty.", "No two ways about it.", "full stop", "Don't reuse marinade. Not once."
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-4 yarn, swearing within the dad dial ("the little mongrels"): "Picture this: picnic and barbie season, snags burnin' and the flies havin' a go".
yarn-troppo.tone: Friendly safety advice stays friendly and practical, the warnings intact: "Don't cross-contaminate." ... "and that's how you end up crook."
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads well, though the emphatic tags pile up: "Raw meat, chook and seafood stay wrapped up tight, full stop.", "Sounds obvious, I know."
yarn-troppo.variety: Plenty of different slang, but "tucker" and "mitts" are leaned on: "Your tucker's got to stay safe", "Keep cold tucker cold", "the cooked tucker", "Food safety starts with your mitts", "make sure your mitts", "give your mitts a going-over".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the picnic food-safety guide, headings and all: "Pack and Transport Your Tucker Safely", "Quick Tips for Setting Up at the Picnic Spot", "Follow Safe Barbie Tips".

yarn-deadset.meaning: Faithful throughout: "Cold tucker should be kept at 40 °F (4 °C) or below to stop bacteria growing.", "Don't reuse marinade.", "have a clean platter and utensils ready next to the barbie".
yarn-deadset.sense: Terms carry the sense: "esky", "chook", "kitchen bench", "tea towel", "tucker that goes off" for perishables, "once you've rocked up".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: The swaps are mechanical, slang dropped into official sentences where no Australian would put it: "Marinate tucker in the fridge", "lets bacteria from the raw tucker's juices spread to the cooked tucker", "Or think about using wet wipes for cleaning your mitts."
yarn-deadset.register: Word swaps on the original's sentences rather than a level-4 retelling: "Think about packing drinks in one esky and tucker that goes off in another. That way, as the picnickers open and reopen the drinks esky to top up their drinks".
yarn-deadset.tone: The guide's helpful, official tone is kept: "Read on for simple food safety guidelines".
yarn-deadset.flow: Readable, but the repetitive swaps clunk: "the tucker that goes off won't be exposed to warm outdoor air temperatures", "Cook tucker right through. When it's time to cook the tucker".
yarn-deadset.variety: "tucker" in nearly every sentence ("Keep your tucker safe", "Put cold tucker in an esky", "Keep \"ready\" tucker hot"), and "heaps" twice in the first two sentences: "offers heaps of chances" ... "give foodborne bacteria heaps of chances".
yarn-deadset.essence: Recognisably the guide, structure intact, but flattened into a substitution: "Pack and Transport Tucker Safely".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All guidelines kept: "Pop your cold tucker in an esky with ice or frozen ice bricks", "open the esky as few times as you can", "If the packet says \"ready-to-eat,\" \"washed,\" or \"triple washed,\" you don't need to wash it.", "Marinate your tucker in the fridge".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Every term fits: "once you've rocked up", "the tucker that goes off isn't copping the warm outdoor air", "No running water handy?", "kitchen bench".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural phrasing: "when everyone's in and out of the drinks esky topping up", "Firm-skinned ones want a rub under running tap water". "tucker" is still dropped in more than a local would.
yarn-dinkum.register: A real retelling but restrained, a little lighter than level 4, no swearing: "Picnic and barbie season's got heaps going for it: plenty of chances to get outdoors and have a bit of fun".
yarn-dinkum.tone: Cheerful and practical, as the original: "Read on for a few simple food safety guidelines".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Once it's done, shift it to the side of the barbie grill, just away from the coals, and it'll stay hot till it's served."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied verbs and openers ("Pop", "Sort out the esky", "No running water handy?"), but "tucker" recurs throughout: "Cook your tucker right through", "the cooked tucker", "the raw tucker's juices".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the guide, retold: "Quick Tips for Setting Up at the Picnic Spot", "Follow Safe Barbie Tips".

engine.meaning: Nothing lost; it is mostly the original: "Cold tucker should be stored at 40 °F or below to prevent bacterial growth.", "Don't reuse platters or utensils."
engine.sense: The swaps mostly fit ("esky", "kitchen bench", "mitts"), though "fronted up" for arriving is a little off, and "perishable tucker" strains.
engine.authenticity: US forms left in beside the swaps: "Organize esky contents.", "Keep coolers closed: Once at the picnic site, limit the number of times the cooler is opened", "Meat, poultry, and seafood", "Follow Safe Grilling Tips".
engine.register: Largely untranslated for level 4: "Food safety begins with proper hand cleaning — including in outdoor settings.", "Or, consider using moist disposable towelettes for cleaning your mitts."
engine.tone: The original's tone is untouched: "there are important guidelines that should be followed".
engine.flow: Jarring joins of official prose and slang, and esky/cooler both used: "Consider packing beverages in one esky and perishable tucker in another.", "before packing them in the cooler".
engine.variety: Only "tucker", "esky", "mitts" and "mates", repeated: "Grilled tucker can be kept hot", "Cook tucker thoroughly."
engine.essence: The original with words swapped: "Clean your produce.", "Quick Tips for Picnic Site Preparation".

unharnessed.meaning: All guidelines kept: "Stick cold food in an esky with ice or frozen gel packs.", "Think about packing the drinks in one esky and the perishables in another.", "set a bit aside separately before the raw meat, chook or seafood goes in", "have your food thermometer handy".
unharnessed.sense: Mostly exact ("copping a dose of food poisoning", "lugging your tucker", "cooked to buggery"), but "out in the bush too" narrows "outdoor settings" to the bush, and "gives the nasty bugs in your tucker a real chance to go off" bends "go off" from food spoiling to bacteria thriving.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian: "all that warm-weather carry-on", "bacteria breed like bloody rabbits", "when everyone's opening and shutting the drinks esky to grab another one", "there's some important rules to stick to".
unharnessed.register: A real retelling with swearing inside the dial ("bloody rabbits", "cooked to buggery"), a touch lighter than A's full yarn, keeping plain "food" in many places: "Keep cold food cold."
unharnessed.tone: Friendly safety advice with its warnings intact: "Don't cross-contaminate. Make sure raw meat, chook and seafood are wrapped up good and tight."
unharnessed.flow: Smooth throughout: "Give fresh fruit and veg a rinse under the running tap before they go in the esky".
unharnessed.variety: Varied, with nothing leaned on: "carry-on", "copping a dose", "lugging", "rocked up", "dishing it up", "good and tight", "to buggery".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the guide, headings kept: "Pack and Transport Food Safely", "Follow Safe Grilling Tips".

summaries.yarn-troppo: A full, faithful level-4 yarn with good colour, leaning hard on "tucker" and "mitts" and a few bolted-on tags.
summaries.yarn-deadset: Accurate but mechanical: a word-swap version leaning on "tucker", too light and stiff for level 4.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: A clean, natural, faithful retelling, a touch light for level 4 and over-reliant on "tucker".
summaries.engine: Mostly the original with a few nouns swapped and US forms left in: inconsistent and far too light for level 4.
summaries.unharnessed: Natural, varied and faithful, a touch lighter than a full level 4, with a couple of strained senses.
